findings.failure_path: A verified chunk for lines 1 through N can end inside row k, and a verified chunk for lines k through N can resume at the next byte of that row. Their union covers the skill. Because spans are merged under separate (first, last) keys, neither range completes row k and the checkpoint can deny an edit after a complete read. The host's continuation hint does not constrain an explicitly supplied range.
findings.smallest_fix: Merge verified intervals in absolute canonical byte coordinates per skill, preserving row-separator handling. Cover this split with a complete-read case and a one-byte-gap control.

findings.failure_path: If revalidation moves after the second write, the bridge can publish through both names, then deny and truncate the held inode during cleanup. Both current assertions still pass. M19 exercises removal of the check, while this ordering regression retains the check and its deny.
findings.smallest_fix: Observe the second write at the write boundary in a focused test and assert that revalidation rejects the linked descriptor before any write occurs. Verify the test fails when revalidation moves immediately after the write.

findings.failure_path: T6f checks only the absence of a Skill event. Restoring the predecessor's eager bytes slice returns the same result, so the test stays green if malformed replay again allocates the full claimed interval while holding the conversation lock.
findings.smallest_fix: Exercise partial_lines with a prebuilt canonical stream, a large non-full interval, and a short body. Measure peak allocation around that call with a bound that the original slice exceeds, then verify the predecessor expression fails the assertion.

findings.failure_path: The generated guard interpolates twin directly into executable shell text twice. A temporary directory containing spaces breaks the fixture, and shell metacharacters in a valid directory name can cause unintended command execution under the test runner's account.
findings.smallest_fix: Quote the interpolated path with shlex.quote before generating the script, or pass it as data through an environment variable and quote its expansion.

concern_results.conclusion: The claimed-interval copy is fixed at line 328. Verified chunks can still cover a whole skill without producing a Skill event when two different range headers split the same row.

The new hardlink fixture preserves the shadow inode, addressing the previous fixture defect. Its final size assertion observes the file after cleanup, so a transient second write remains undetectable through that assertion. The fixture also embeds a filesystem path directly into shell source.

Python short-circuits on a body-length mismatch after the UTF-8 start adjustment. Equal-length bodies use a memoryview without copying the claimed interval. The packet lacks the lock, sweep, and cleanup callers needed to trace failures while a shadow is populated.

T6f would pass with the original copying expression. T4e exercises the previously missing hardlink case, and M19 reports sensitivity to removing the cached-descriptor check. T4e does not establish when the denial happened relative to the second write.

The runtime edit adds no flag, permission, or deployment step. The documented restriction that fragments completing a row must share a requested line range has no counterpart in the acceptance criterion.

The runtime delta changes an in-memory comparison and requires no data migration. Reverting it restores the allocation risk during replay. The packet does not establish current-candidate release verification.
A final deny and an empty file are observable. Neither identifies the failing guard or establishes that the denial preceded publication. The packet also omits the exception-to-verdict path.

The host continuation hint supports the usual same-range workflow. It does not exclude another valid range request. The 58-test result and M19 outcome are reported results. This static review did not rerun them.

The comparison requires matching canonical bytes for the interval shown. The hardlink acceptance criterion also requires rejection before writing through the extra name, which remains a timing gap in the test.

The quoted contracts require deterministic hook validation and a completion record bound to the current candidate. The disposition points to Local Verification, but the frozen packet omits the current full-lane outcome and identifies only the predecessor commit.
